excerpt: Paano magtanim ng sibuyas tagalog? Here is how traditional Filipino farmers usually plant sibuyas Tagalog (shallot), step by step from getting the field ready to the harvest, with the day of each step and what to change for a higher yield.

heroImage.alt: A farm worker planting in a field

blocks.title: This is the traditional way
blocks.text: This guide shows how traditional farmers usually plant sibuyas Tagalog. Use it as a starting point. For a higher yield, update it: plant certified seed or clean planting material, test your soil, and follow the right spacing and fertilizer.

How Filipino farmers grow sibuyas tagalog, the small red multiplier onion called lasona in Ilocos, planted from bulbs in rice fields after the harvest. Each bulb splits into a clump of new bulbs in about three months.

Before you plant, get the field ready with our [land preparation guide for onion and garlic](/land-preparation/onion-garlic-land-preparation). Then choose your seed or planting material with the [sibuyas Tagalog nutrient deficiency guide](/nutrient-deficiencies/shallot-nutrient-deficiency).
When to plant sibuyas Tagalog
Planted after the rice harvest, from about October to December in the Ilocos Region and Central Luzon, and pulled from about January to March.
What you plant

Bulbs from the last harvest, cured and kept hanging in bundles until they are ready to sprout. Farmers split the clumps into single bulbs and often cut off the top part to make them sprout faster. About a ton of bulbs is planted on a hectare.
Paano magtanim ng sibuyas tagalog, step by step
The crop is ready about 85 days after sowing.
Before planting (Bago magtanim)

items.title: 7 days before sowing: Prepare the field
items.text: After the rice harvest, cut the stubble close to the ground, or plow, harrow and make beds. Mix in manure or compost.

items.title: 1 day before sowing: Split and trim the bulbs
items.text: Split the clumps into single firm bulbs, throw out soft or moldy ones, and cut off the top part of each bulb.

blocks.text: Planting day (Pagtatanim)

items.title: Sowing day: Fertilizer before planting
items.text: Spread complete fertilizer (14 14 14) over the field or beds.

items.title: Sowing day: Plant the bulbs
items.text: Push the bulbs into moist soil about 15 to 20 cm apart each way, with the cut top just at the surface.

items.title: Sowing day: Mulch with rice straw
items.text: Spread rice straw thinly over the field to keep in moisture and hold back weeds.

blocks.text: Care while it grows (Pag aalaga)

items.title: Day 2: Water
items.text: Let water into the field or the canals until the soil is wet, then drain. Repeat every week or so in the dry months.

items.title: Day 25: Side dress
items.text: Side dress urea (46 0 0) or ammonium sulfate (21 0 0) and water it in.

items.title: Day 30: Watch for armyworm and leaf diseases
items.text: Check the leaves for caterpillars, egg masses, thrips and purple blotch, and pick off egg masses by hand.

items.title: Day 45: Feed as the bulbs form
items.text: Give complete fertilizer (14 14 14), often with potash (0 0 60), as the clumps start to swell.

items.title: Day 70: Stop watering
items.text: Stop watering about two weeks before harvest.

blocks.text: Harvest (Anihan)

items.title: Day 85: Pull the clumps
items.text: Harvest when most leaves have yellowed and fallen over. Pull the clumps by hand.

items.title: Day 86: Dry, bundle and hang
items.text: Dry the clumps in the field for a few days, then tie them in bundles by the leaves and hang them in an airy shed. Keep the best bulbs for the next planting.

parts.title: Dry the clumps in the field
parts.text: Lay the pulled clumps on the dry field with the leaves of one row over the bulbs of the row before, so the sun does not scald them. Carry them under a roof if rain comes.

parts.title: Tie bundles by the leaves
parts.text: When the leaves are dry and limp, shake off the soil and tie the clumps in bundles by their leaves.

parts.title: Hang them in an airy shed
parts.text: Hang the bundles on bamboo poles under the house or in a shed where air moves, out of the sun and rain. Some hang them above the kitchen stove, where the smoke helps dry them and keeps insects off.

parts.title: Keep the best for planting
parts.text: Set aside bundles of firm, medium to big bulbs from the healthiest clumps. They stay hanging until the bulbs begin to show sprouts, the sign they are ready to plant again.

parts.title: Check the bundles
parts.text: Look the bundles over every couple of weeks and pull out bulbs that are soft, moldy or rotting before they spread to the rest.

blocks.text: Spacing, water and fertilizer for sibuyas Tagalog
Spacing
Bulbs about 15 to 20 cm apart each way, in the field after rice or on beds.
Water
Watered by letting water into the field or canals and draining it, about every week in the dry months, and stopped two weeks before harvest.
Fertilizer

Manure or compost at land preparation, complete fertilizer (14 14 14) at planting, urea (46 0 0) or ammonium sulfate (21 0 0) at about three to four weeks, and complete fertilizer with potash (0 0 60) as the bulbs form. To read what a bag really gives, see our guide to [fertilizer for this crop](/blog/fertilizer-for-vegetables-philippines).
Care and harvest
Care while it grows
Light rice straw mulch, hand weeding, and watching for armyworm, thrips and leaf blotch.
When and how to harvest
Ready at about 70 to 90 days, when most leaves yellow and fall over. Clumps are pulled, dried for a few days, bundled and hung to cure. The best bulbs are kept for the next planting.
Common mistakes when planting sibuyas Tagalog

items: Planting bulbs from a diseased crop, which carries the disease into the new field.
Planting freshly harvested bulbs that are not yet ready to sprout.
Letting water stand in the field.
Storing clumps that are not fully cured.

blocks.text: How to get a higher yield of sibuyas Tagalog
The traditional way gets a crop, but small changes add up. These are the first things to change, one season at a time.

items: Use clean, firm planting bulbs, ideally from a disease free source.
Plant on time after the rice harvest so the crop ripens before the summer rains.
Feed by a soil test and keep the field well drained.
Pick armyworm egg masses early and scout every week.
